name: bdx_inspired_original_v1
cadence_note: single_support_duration sets the stride period exactly: period = 2.4 * single_support_duration (the generator quantises to single_support_timesteps=10 plus round(double_support_ratio*10)=2, so 2*(10+2) timesteps of ssd/10 each). It must stay at 0.225, giving the 0.540 s period the neutral checkpoint is trained on. Cadence is not one of the five style traits, and changing it is not a style choice: the imitation reward's joint_pos term is an unbounded quadratic on joint angles, so a policy whose stride cannot phase-lock to the reference clock scores strictly worse than one that stops walking and sits near the reference mean pose. Style fine-tuning from a cadence-mismatched reference therefore collapses to marching in place, with no gradient path back to walking. Verified: at a 0.540 s clock the 220M neutral policy scores -0.79 on joint_pos, versus -1.80 at every other period and -1.26 for a standing policy.
joint_limit_note: walk_foot_height 0.02 and 0.04 were both validated by generate()'s self-check (both knees bend in the natural/positive direction, and JointRangeChecker's RANGE_TOLERANCE of 0.5 rad past the model's +/-1.5708 rad range is the accepted overshoot -- see AGENTS.md's reference motion invariants). 0.06 has not been generated yet; the upstream generator disables IK joint limits, so raising walk_foot_height further is not guaranteed to validate and generate() will self-check it and retry with a small walk_com_height nudge before failing loudly. Lowering walk_com_height or feet_spacing has the same effect on required knee flexion as raising walk_foot_height, and is worth trying together if walk_foot_height alone stops improving the incentive margin.
baseline_note: These are the generator's placo_defaults values, except single_support_duration. placo_defaults says 0.17, but the shipped reference the neutral stages actually train against has a 0.540 s period, i.e. ssd 0.225. Treating 0.17 as the baseline and nudging to 0.18 silently cut the stride period by 20% and was what made the first three style seeds stop walking. The baseline that matters is the trained checkpoint's cadence, not the generator's default.
